---
title: "Getting started"
output: html_document
---

Draw arrival counts, check available places, then generate the admitted people.
Your functions supply all individual attributes and stay dates.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## Define places

`make_landscape()` gives one row per location, with `n` places.
This example uses hospitals, wards and rooms.

```{r}
library(nososim)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
devtools::load_all()
hospital <- list(
  H1 = list(
    A = c(a = 2, b = 3),
    B = c(a = 1, b = 4, c = 2)
  ),
  H2 = list(
    A = c(a = 3, b = 5),
    B = c(a = 2, b = 4, c = 1)
  )
)
landscape <- make_landscape(hospital)
```

## Draw attempted arrivals

`admissions()` returns one count per location. Here each location has one
attempted arrival per day. The simulator limits these counts to free places.

```{r}
admissions <- function(landscape, date) {
  rep(1L, nrow(landscape))
}
```

## Generate admitted individuals

`individuals()` receives one row per allocated place. It creates complete
records for those people: location columns, `start` (today), `end` (a later date),
and any attributes you choose. Nobody is generated for a blocked arrival.

```{r}
individuals <- function(locations, date) {
  locations |>
    mutate(
      id = paste0(format(date, "%Y%m%d"), "_", row_number()),
      age = sample(18:90, n(), replace = TRUE),
      role = "patient",
      start = date,
      end = start + if_else(location_2 == "A", 2L, 3L)
    )
}
```

The IDs, attributes and stay dates above are all user-defined. A separate `los`
column is optional; the simulator only needs the location columns and period.

## Run

```{r}
dates <- as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:6
set.seed(123)
population <- make_population(
  landscape,
  dates,
  admissions = admissions,
  individuals = individuals
)
population |>
  select(id, starts_with("location_"), age, role, start, end) |>
  head(10)
```

The simulation starts empty. Places become free on `end`, before that day's
arrivals. The output contains admitted records only, including people who have
since left. Blocked attempts leave; later arrivals can use places as they become free.

## Optional location parameters

Additional columns are interpreted by your functions. For example, `rate` below
is a user-chosen parameter for Poisson arrivals per location per day.

```{r}
rate_landscape <- landscape |>
  mutate(rate = if_else(location_2 == "A", 0.8, 1.2))

random_admissions <- function(landscape, date) {
  rpois(nrow(landscape), landscape$rate)
}

rate_population <- make_population(
  rate_landscape,
  dates,
  admissions = random_admissions,
  individuals = individuals
)

```

## Plot stays

Each row is an available place, grouped by nested location labels. Stays run
from `start` to `end`; grey lines retain places that are empty.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
autoplot(rate_population, aes(colour = id)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
